# ezghcloud_hosted_queue_rabbitmq_binding (Resource)

A binding from an exchange to a queue or exchange on a RabbitMQ cluster. Any change replaces it. Destroying it deletes this binding alone.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster (hqc_) it is in. Changing it replaces the object.
- `destination` (String) The queue or exchange it routes to. Changing it replaces the object.
- `destination_type` (String) queue or exchange. Changing it replaces the object.
- `project_id` (String) Project of the cluster. Changing it replaces the object.
- `source` (String) The exchange it routes from. Changing it replaces the object.
- `vhost` (String) The vhost it is in: / (or default) for the default vhost. Changing it replaces the object.

### Optional

- `arguments` (String) Arguments as a JSON object (jsonencode), at most 32 entries. Changing them replaces the object.
- `routing_key` (String) The routing key; empty when left out. Changing it replaces the binding.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) cluster_id/name, with the vhost before the name for a RabbitMQ object.
- `key` (String) The binding's key, assigned by EZGH from its fields.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `origin` (String) api if it was made through EZGH, broker if an app made it first (an imported object).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_hosted_queue_rabbitmq_binding.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/CLUSTER_ID/VHOST/KEY'
```
